info.name: ServiceTrade API
info.description:
The ServiceTrade API is a RESTful web service that allows interaction with the ServiceTrade platform.

# Getting Started

## Authentication

Unless otherwise noted, all API endpoints require authentication. The API supports two authentication methods:

1. **OAuth2 Client Credentials** (Recommended) - Use your client ID and secret to obtain a bearer token from the **[Oauth2Token](/api/docs/tag/oauth2token)** resource
2. **Session Cookie** - Legacy username/password based method using the `PHPSESSID` cookie from the **[Authentication](/api/docs/tag/authentication)** resource

## Permissions

ServiceTrade uses a role-based permission system. Each user is assigned one or more **roles**, and each role grants a set of **activities** (permissions) that determine what actions the user can perform.

**How Permissions Work**

- API requests inherit the permissions of the authenticated user
- Many API resources/actions require specific activities to be granted to the authenticated user
- If a user lacks the required permissions, the API returns HTTP 403 (Forbidden)

**Common Permission Patterns**

Activities are organized by resource type (e.g., `job.manage`, `invoice.view`, `quote.edit`).

| Pattern       | Description                                               |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `*.view`      | Read access to a resource type                            |
| `*.edit`      | Create and modify resources                               |
| `*.manage`    | Full control including workflow actions                   |
| `admin.*`     | Administrative access bypassing record-level restrictions |

**Checking Permissions**

To retrieve the current user's permissions, use the following resources:
- For OAuth2 client credentials-based authentication: first get user details, including user ID, from `GET /oauth2/userinfo`, then fetch `activities` from `GET /user/{userId}/activity`.
- For legacy session-based authentication: first get the user ID from `GET /auth`, then fetch the full user details including `roles` and `activities` from `GET /user/{userId}`.

Use the **[Role](/api/docs/tag/role)** resource to list available roles and their associated activities.


## Requests

An API request consists of an HTTP verb (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`), an endpoint host (`https://api.servicetrade.com/api`), a resource URI (e.g., `/invoice/123`), optional query parameters, and optional request body data.

Request bodies must be valid JSON and sent with `Content-Type: application/json`.

All PUT endpoints support partial updates. You only need to include the fields you want to change; fields not provided retain their current values.

## Response Format

All API responses are JSON with these properties:

| Property              | Description                                             |

item.name: Account
item.description:
The account resource is used to retrieve account settings for the currently authenticated user's account.

This is a read-only resource. POST, PUT, and DELETE operations are not supported.

An account's `primeCompany` is the primary vendor company in each account. It should be used as the `vendor` on contracts, jobs, invoices, and other business entities. All users with UI access must belong to this company. Locations belonging to this company are displayed as offices in the UI.

request.description: Returns the account for the currently authenticated user. This endpoint does not support pagination and always returns exactly one account.
Returns detailed information about a specific account. Users can only access their own account.

item.name: AccountSettings
item.description:
Account settings control various configuration options for your ServiceTrade account.

This endpoint does not support pagination.

request.description: Returns all account settings for the current account. TimeCard-related settings are only included if the account has the TimeCard feature enabled.

variable.description: Name of the setting to update (e.g., `jobTypes`, `timeCardArchive`)

request.description:
Updates a single account setting by name. The setting name is specified in the URI path, and the new value is provided in the request body.

Different settings require different permissions:
- Most settings require `admin.account` permission
- TimeCard settings require `timecard.settings`, `admin.account`, or `admin.user` permission
- `stacConnectorKey` requires `admin.account`, `admin.user`, or `timecard.settings` permission

Not all account settings can be updated through the API.

TimeCard settings (those prefixed with `timeCard`) require the TimeCard feature to be enabled on the account.

The list of `assetDefinitions` options is available by retrieving the **[AssetDefinition](/api/docs/tag/assetdefinition)** list.

item.name: Activity
item.description:
Activities represent available permissions that can be assigned to user roles. Each activity defines a specific capability or action that users can perform within the system, such as `job.manage` or `location.edit`.

Use this endpoint to retrieve the list of permissions available in your account, which you can then assign to roles using the **[Role](/api/docs/tag/role)** endpoint.

request.description: Returns all available activities (permissions) that can be assigned to user roles in your account. This endpoint does not support pagination.
Returns detailed information about a specific activity/permission.

item.name: Asset
item.description:
Assets represent physical equipment, systems, or components at a location that require service or inspection. Assets can be organized hierarchically (parent/child relationships) and associated with services (service requests), task lists, and deficiencies.

Use the `locationId`, `jobId`, `appointmentId`, or time-bound parameters (`createdBefore`, `createdAfter`, `updatedBefore`, `updatedAfter`, `taskTemplateId`) to query for assets. At least one of these parameters is required.

The `properties` object on each asset is a list of key/value pairs representing the asset-type-specific attributes of that asset (manufacturer name, serial number, size, etc). The specific properties available for each asset type can be retrieved from the **[AssetDefinition](/api/docs/tag/assetdefinition)** endpoint.

**Convenience endpoint:** `GET /location/{id}/asset` returns a list of assets at the given location. This is equivalent to `GET /asset?locationId={id}`.

Creates task lists for all subassets of an abstract asset group that are compatible with tasking templates in your account. The templates are automatically selected based on their coverage of the asset types within the group.

- Account must have the Tasking feature enabled
- User must have `tasking.edit` permission

- Subassets without a compatible template will not have task lists created
- When multiple templates apply to the same asset types, the earliest-created template is used

item.name: AssetDefinition

Asset definitions describe the types of assets that can be tracked in ServiceTrade. Each definition specifies the properties, validation rules, and hierarchy for a particular type of asset (e.g., fire alarm, extinguisher, HVAC system). Individual **[Asset](/api/docs/tag/asset)** entities are instances of asset definitions.

Use the `properties` field to understand what data can be stored on assets of each type. The `parentAssetTypes` field defines the hierarchy relationships between asset types.

Use the `instanceName` field to describe how each asset instance's name should be displayed. item.name: Attachment
item.description:
Attachments are files (documents, images, audio, video, etc.) attached to entities such as jobs, locations, assets, quotes, and more.

Uploading attachments works differently than other resources. The binary file data must be sent as part of a `multipart/form-data` POST request. Metadata fields are sent as form fields alongside the file. To send a `meta` field, create a form field like: `<input name="meta[fieldName]" />`.

**Visibility:** Specific attachment types may have additional visibility options beyond the standard ones documented here.

**Malware scanning:** Uploaded attachments may be subjected to a malware scan before they are stored and made available at the attachment's `contentUrl`. Use the `scanStatus` property to determine the current malware scan status of an attachment.

**Supported Entities:** Attachments can be added to **[Asset](/api/docs/tag/asset)**, **[Brand](/api/docs/tag/brand)**, **[ChangeOrder](/api/docs/tag/changeorder)**, **[Company](/api/docs/tag/company)*

item.name: Authentication
item.description:
The authentication endpoints are used to create and manage API sessions. It creates a session token that must be sent along with any request to a protected resource.

The ServiceTrade API uses HTTP cookies to maintain an authenticated session. After successfully authenticating with a `POST` request to the Authentication endpoint, the HTTP client should include the returned `authToken` as a `PHPSESSID` cookie on each subsequent request. If the cookie is not sent on a request to a resource that requires an authenticated session, the request will fail.

For more information, see the [Authentication](/api/docs/description/authentication) documentation.

**Session limits:** There is a soft limit of 100 concurrent sessions per user, and a hard limit of 200. If the limit of 200 concurrent sessions is exceeded, the oldest sessions will be pruned up to the soft limit (100).

request.description: Returns authentication information for the currently logged-in user. If no active session exists, returns a `404` error.

Authenticates a user with username and password. On success, creates a new session and returns user details with a session token (`authToken`).

**Note:** The POST (create session) endpoint does not require authentication to access.
Terminates the current authenticated session. Returns `204` on success with no content body.

Authenticates a user using OAuth2 tokens (`id_token` and `access_token`) from the Identity Provider (Auth0). On success, creates a new session and returns user details. Optionally accepts a `refresh_token` which will be stored for future use.

For users with multiple accounts sharing the same email, an optional `user_id` parameter can be provided to select a specific user account.

item.name: Budget
item.description:
Budgets track estimated costs and prices for project jobs. Each budget exists as a chain of versions, grouped by reference number, where each version represents a point-in-time snapshot. Budgets can be either high-level (using **[BudgetCategory](/api/docs/tag/budgetcategory)**) or granular (using **[BudgetLineItem](/api/docs/tag/budgetlineitem)**).

`high_level` budgets are deprecated and can no longer be created in the UI.

Change order categories are only used with high-level budgets. For granular budgets, use **[ChangeOrderLineItem](/api/docs/tag/changeorderlineitem)** instead.

item.description:

item.description:
Invoice recurrences define recurring billing schedules for a location. They automatically generate **[Invoice](/api/docs/tag/invoice)** records on a specified frequency (monthly or yearly) at defined intervals. The `endsOn` property indicates the date after which no additional invoices should be generated. The `nextDue` property indicates the date on which the next invoice will be generated.

- **Expired:** The `endsOn` is in the past. There may be uninvoiced items (if `nextDue` is earlier than `endsOn`).

The Recurring Invoices section of the location page UI will only show Active invoice recurrences.

item.name: Webhook
item.description:
Webhooks allow a system that integrates with the ServiceTrade API to receive notifications about updated data without polling. When an entity changes, a notification message is sent to a specified URL containing enough data to identify the entity, so the integrated system can request more data from the appropriate API endpoint.

An account can set up more than one webhook. Each webhook independently receives each notification message that is sent.

**Webhook Requirements**

In order to receive messages, the webhook URL MUST:

- **Be publicly accessible** - The webhook URL must be available on the public Internet; ServiceTrade cannot send messages to internal URLs.
- **Accept HTTP POST requests** - Each message is sent as an HTTP POST request to the webhook URL.
- **Respond with HTTP status code between 200-499** - If the status code is outside this range (or not received within 5 seconds), the message will be retried. After 3 unsuccessful attempts, the message will be discarded.
